**Section D: Essay (10 marks).** Write an essay of about 250-300 words on ONE of the following topics.

**Topic 1.** Give a talk to fellow students on the importance of contributing to the development of your homeland instead of travelling abroad illegally.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
La rédaction anglaise du BAC série A évalue à la fois le respect du format imposé (discours, lettre formelle, récit personnel) et la qualité du contenu : un texte au contenu riche mais mal formaté perd des points que ni les idées ni la grammaire ne peuvent compenser. Le sujet proposant un choix, un seul texte doit être rédigé le jour de l'examen ; les modèles ci-dessous illustrent chacun des trois sujets proposés. Le sujet 3, portant sur le VIH/SIDA, est un thème classique d'éducation à la santé dans ce type d'épreuve : il doit être traité avec sérieux, sans détail médical superflu ni stigmatisation, en insistant sur le dépistage, la prise en charge et l'espoir d'une vie saine avec un traitement adapté.

## Topic 1 - Speech (modèle, environ 260 mots)

Dear friends,

I stand before you today to talk about a choice many young Cameroonians face: whether to build their future here, at home, or to seek it abroad, sometimes through dangerous and illegal means.

I understand the appeal of leaving. Stories of opportunity overseas are everywhere, and for some, the difficulties of daily life here make emigration feel like the only path to success. But I ask you to consider the real cost of illegal travel: countless young people have lost their lives attempting perilous journeys across deserts and seas, while others who arrive safely find themselves without papers, without rights, and without the dignity they hoped to gain.

Staying does not mean giving up on ambition. Our country needs engineers, doctors, teachers and entrepreneurs who understand its realities and are willing to build within it rather than abandon it. Every road built, every school opened, every business started here is a brick laid in our nation's future — and each of us has a role to play in laying those bricks.

This does not mean opportunities abroad should never be pursued; they should simply be pursued legally and safely, through proper channels such as scholarships, visas and formal work programmes, not through smugglers who profit from our desperation.

Friends, our homeland needs us more than any foreign shore does. Let us choose to build it together, safely and with dignity.

Thank you.

**Section D: Essay (10 marks).** Write an essay of about 250-300 words on ONE of the following topics.

**Topic 2.** Write a letter to your school principal to persuade him/her to connect the school to the internet. Your name is Ateba Clara, of St Peter and Paul College Kumba, P.O. Box 628 Kumba.
questions.corrige_markdown:
## Topic 2 - Formal letter (modèle, environ 230 mots)

Ateba Clara
St Peter and Paul College Kumba
P.O. Box 628
Kumba

The Principal
St Peter and Paul College Kumba

Subject: Request for internet connection in the school

Dear Sir,

I am writing on behalf of my classmates to request that our school be connected to the internet, as I believe this would greatly benefit our education.

Many of the research assignments given by our teachers require information that our current library, however well-stocked, simply cannot provide, particularly on recent scientific and technological developments. Students in better-equipped schools already have access to online resources, educational videos, and past examination papers, which places them at a clear advantage over us.

An internet connection would also allow our teachers to access modern teaching materials and communicate more easily with educational partners and examination bodies. Beyond academics, it would help prepare us for a world where digital skills are increasingly essential for further studies and employment.

I understand that installing and maintaining such a connection involves costs, and I would be glad if the school could explore options such as partnerships with telecommunication companies or educational programmes that support connectivity in schools.

I hope you will give this request your favourable consideration, and I remain available to discuss it further with the school administration.

Yours faithfully,

Ateba Clara

**Section D: Essay (10 marks).** Write an essay of about 250-300 words on ONE of the following topics.

**Topic 3.** You discovered, after taking an HIV/AIDS test, that you are positive. Narrate how you felt and what you did about it. What advice would you give to young people on managing their sexual life so as to protect their health?
questions.corrige_markdown:
## Topic 3 - Narrative essay (modèle, environ 280 mots)

*Note pédagogique : ce sujet aborde le VIH/SIDA sous l'angle du dépistage, de la prise en charge médicale et de la prévention — thème sensible mais classique du programme d'éducation à la santé, traité ici sans détail médical intrusif et sans stigmatisation, dans un esprit d'information et d'espoir.*

The day I received the results of my HIV test remains etched in my memory. I sat in the small consulting room, my hands trembling slightly, as the counsellor explained that the test had come back positive. For a moment, I felt as though the walls were closing in around me; fear, shame and disbelief all arrived at once, and I wondered whether my life, as I had imagined it, was over.

The counsellor, however, spoke calmly and reassured me that a positive result was not a death sentence. She explained that with early treatment, a healthy diet, and consistent care, people living with HIV today lead long, full and productive lives. She encouraged me to begin antiretroviral treatment immediately and to keep to my appointments without fail.

In the weeks that followed, I chose to confide in my mother and one close friend, both of whom offered me support rather than judgement. Slowly, my fear gave way to determination: I was not going to let this diagnosis define or limit who I was.

Looking back, I would advise every young person to take charge of their sexual health long before facing such a moment. Get tested regularly, remain faithful to one partner or use protection consistently, avoid sharing sharp objects, and never be afraid to seek medical advice early. Above all, remember that a diagnosis is not a judgement of your worth: with the right care and support, it is entirely possible to remain healthy and to live a fulfilling life.

### Piège à éviter
Sur ce type de sujet sensible, l'erreur la plus grave serait de sombrer dans un ton misérabiliste, moralisateur ou stigmatisant envers les personnes séropositives : le sujet attend un récit réaliste mais digne, qui montre qu'un diagnostic de VIH n'est ni une honte ni une fatalité lorsque la prise en charge médicale est suivie.

### Conseil
Pour les sujets de santé sensibles, structure toujours ta réponse en trois temps : la réaction émotionnelle initiale (honnête mais sans excès dramatique), les démarches concrètes entreprises (consultation, traitement, soutien), puis un message de prévention constructif à l'attention des autres jeunes.

incertitudes: Le sujet 3 aborde un thème de santé sensible (annonce d'une séropositivité) ; le corrigé proposé volontairement facteul, non stigmatisant et centré sur la prise en charge médicale et la prévention, conformément aux bonnes pratiques d'éducation à la santé, plutôt que sur des détails intrusifs ou dramatisés.
